To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Salmonella spp. is widely distributed in the different points of the slaughter chain of free-range pigs and the cross-contamination of different serotypes was observed in different points of the chain, pointing to an important risk of contamination for pork from free-range systems.
Salmonella spp. was detected in different points of the slaughtering chain of free-range pigs, and that different strains belonging to different epidemiological sources were isolated.
Salmonella spp. was isolated in all points sampled in the slaughtering chain from pigs reared free-range systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection, isolation, identification and characterization of Salmonella spp in free-range pigs and the environmental contamination in the slaughtering chain.
the detection of Salmonella in a slaughterhouse from pigs reared under free-range systems, as well as with the identification of different epidemiological origins of the isolates.
the detection of the prevalence and characterization of Salmonella spp in a free-range pork chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of Salmonella in pigs and the environment of free-range pigs, as well as in the pork derived from them is a serious risk factor for foodborne illness, especially when the slaughtering process is not properly managed and controlled.
Salmonella spp. can be present in free-range pigs and that it is important to control the contamination of pigs and their environment in order to prevent the risk of contamination in pork products.
the prevalence of Salmonellae is high in pigs reared in a free-range system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of Salmonella at the pre-slaughter phase of the pig chain (i.e. in trucks and lairage) represents a great risk for post-slaughter contamination of the carcass.
Salmonella spp. are still an important risk for the food chain and a great challenge for pork industry.
the prevalence of Salmonellae in the free-range system is similar to other production systems and that the risk of cross-contamination is present.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of Salmonellosis is present in free range systems and the control of the risk of contamination should be considered.
the presence of Salmonella in pigs reared in organic systems is not a negligible issue, and that the implementation of adequate bio-security practices is essential to reduce or eliminate this risk.
Salmonella spp. are still a great threat in the slaughtering process of free-range pigs, even if the prevalence of this pathogen is not as high as in conventional pigs.
